# Fixed Lamport v1 compatibility vectors

These files are **frozen compatibility test data**. They are checked-in
golden bytes for the v1 Lamport private-key, public-key, signature and
one-time-signer checkpoint encodings and must never be regenerated by
the test suite.

- `bits7/`, `bits256/` — the Lamport `bits` parameter (14 key elements
  and a 7-element signature for `bits=7`; 512 key elements and a
  256-element signature for `bits=256`).
- `private_key.bin` — `PrivateKey.to_bytes()` of the deterministic key.
  Contains the secret in the clear; these are public, non-secret test
  values.
- `public_key.bin` — `PublicKey.to_bytes()` of the matching public key.
- `signature.bin` — `lamport_signature_to_bytes(signature, bits=bits)`
  of the signature over the fixed message `b"compat-lamport-v1"` with
  no context.
- `checkpoint_unused.bin` — `OneTimeSigner.checkpoint()` before any
  signature (`used = 0`).
- `checkpoint_used.bin` — `checkpoint()` immediately after signing
  `b"compat-lamport-v1"` (`used = 1`).

## Deterministic key input

The keys come from the public `keygen(bits=bits, token_bytes=...)` entry
with a repeatable `token_bytes` (no real secret material): the first
call returns the integer 1 as a 32-byte big-endian value, the second
call the integer 2, and so on, incrementing by one per call in secret
order (`keygen` draws `2 * bits` secrets). Each `bits` value starts
from its own independent counter. These are public, non-secret test
values, so every sample can be re-derived and reviewed independently.

The exact bytes were produced once by a standalone script using the
baseline encoder and are now fixed; tests only read them. If a future
change to the v1 encodings, the digest/secret derivation or the
checkpoint state handling makes any of these bytes mismatch, that is
the compatibility break the regression test exists to catch — it must
not be silently fixed by relaxing parsing or regenerating these files.
